dedupe_keys.name: collaborative research shear buckling mechanics for enhanced performance of thin plates

description: Collaborative Research: Shear-Buckling Mechanics for Enhanced Performance of Thin Plates is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Maria Garlock, Princeton University (princeton.edu). Thin steel plates are commonly used as structural elements in buildings, bridges, towers, aircrafts, etc. Due to their slenderness, these plates are susceptible to buckling under shear loading, thus limiting their capacity. The project description reports that many existing models do not represent the mechanics of ultimate shear buckling. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Keywords: Shear buckling,  plate girders,  large-scale,  flat web,  low-frequency sinusoidal web,  three-point bending. Published 2025-02-03. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
